rationale:
Independent implementation review of the author16->author17 mechanical-recovery change at source 3577bcca. The diagnosis is sound and matches original source: author16 completed with native transport_returncode 0 but has no accepted-author event and the state is BLOCKED with reason OUTPUT_VALIDATION_REFUSED: NOTEBOOK_EXECUTION_ENTRYPOINT:synthetic_tests (MECHANICAL_DIAGNOSIS: two top-level synthetic_tests definitions). notebook_execution.extract/entrypoints requires len(entries)==1 undecorated zero-arg synthetic_tests, so this is a genuine author contract failure, not a controller defect.

The repair is tightly scoped. In item4_scoped_calls.connect the accepted-author prerequisite is bypassed only on the exact failed16->17 edge (diagnostic_recovery is not None and len(tail)==6 and stage=='run_spec_author' and tail[-1]['id']==FAILED_AUTHOR), then item4_smoke_response.failed_author re-qualifies it: the FAILED_AUTHOR row must be COMPLETE in both manual and global ledgers, have no author-accepted event, match the recorded output_sha256 and native console_sha256, native returncode 0, and a workspace of run_spec_author-16 with unchanged failed outputs. reviewer13 still requires accepted17 (connect_roles ACCEPTED_AUTHOR), and the whole-plan interpretation pair still requires ordinary experiment_collection.verified — confirmed by test_recovery_... which shows the final result_interpretation_author reserve raising and the first 28 call rows preserved. Caps move one slot along the existing gated prefix chain to 32 local / 70 batch (RECOVERY_SCHEMA profile, dispatch_limiter now allows 32, test asserts run_limit=32/batch_limit=70); daily 50 unchanged; $25/$150/$1200/$1275 diagnostic authority matches OPERATOR_DECISION and is re-checked in scope(); automatic_retry False; execution_authorized forced False in proof/activate/finish_review and the fixture unit has no cleanup timer and NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict.

The same-call entrypoint feedback factors entrypoints() out of extract() with identical check logic (host extract remains authoritative) and reuses it via author_output_schema.visible_module, which reconstructs only fully visible writefile cells, refuses omitted/partial/duplicate/malformed entrypoints and out-of-span edits, and binds the view/manifest by sha. The sender path (send/author_sender_admitted) requires matching RUNNING local+global admissions and the exact pending binding before calling the existing send_bound; the command must equal af.client_command(base) with approval_policy=never and network_access=false, and only a read-only bind of the runtime is added — preparing the validator cannot itself admit a call. Sender tests confirm refusal without ledger mutation for local/global missing, complete, uncertain, pending, input, and wrong-call faults.

Across the six fixed categories I find nothing unresolved: budget/metric — caps and dollar authority unchanged, no new spend; execution authority/provenance — protected execution-authority keys preserved, host extraction/synthetic-test gate authoritative, installer requires both the implementation APPROVE and the direction APPROVE (ddcdc756) and stays install-held, cold replay shows provider_calls/model_calls/live_ledger_mutations 0 and is labeled SIMULATED_TEST_ONLY; test-set/leakage — synthetic-only, tests_passed forbids skipped>0, no patient/final/reserve data, network isolated; privacy/secret — no credential creation/change/print, subscription-only transport; code/spec mismatch — controller behavior, contract guidance, recorded refusal, and tests are mutually consistent. This is the shortest safe path: it reuses the existing validator/runtime/installer rather than adding a new proof subsystem. My independent judgment, not the prior-session reference, drives this APPROVE; findings are empty.
